concept: Zone sharding and region-aware shard keys

claims.text: The documented {country: 1, userid: 1} design uses country for regional zones and userid for higher cardinality and lower value frequency than country alone. A region-only key forfeits that finer distribution component. (low confidence)

In the documented country-prefixed design, including country lets reads target the relevant shard subset; omitting country broadcasts reads. A regional zone can contain multiple shards, so providing only the regional prefix does not guarantee a single-shard query. (medium confidence)

Historical bug SERVER-73848 documented conflicting old and new config.tags ranges, or duplicate-key errors, when resharding from a hashed key to the same field without hashing. The issue records fixes in 5.0.19, 6.0.7, 7.0.0-rc3 and 7.1.0-rc0; this is historical upgrade evidence, not proof that current releases retain the defect. (low confidence)

The 2021 University of Piraeus study of spatio-temporal MongoDB workloads used zones to preserve locality and found that fewer nodes processed some queries. Several larger queries became slower because reduced parallelism increased work per participating node; this workload-specific result is not a benchmark of regional deployment costs. (low confidence)

A geographic field must lead the shard key when zones partition directly by geographic location: zone bounds must contain the shard-key prefix and cannot use fields outside the shard key. (medium confidence)
Zone ranges include their lower bound and exclude their upper bound, and ranges cannot overlap. Boundary tests should include exact endpoints when validating regional mappings. (medium confidence)

Changing zone assignments does not relocate existing data immediately: placement may violate the new policy until balancing completes. Treat the transition as a placement-verification requirement rather than assuming that successful configuration means immediate residency. (medium confidence)

A zone can cover multiple country values: MongoDB's location tutorial places both UK and DE in one EU zone. This permits regional resource sharing instead of requiring a separate shard or zone for every country. (low confidence)

Zone sharding associates shard-key ranges with one or more eligible shards; a shard may belong to multiple zones. In a balanced cluster, data covered by a zone resides on shards assigned to that zone. (medium confidence)

The cost-lever inference is to include the geographic prefix in frequent regional reads and confirm targeting with explain(): avoiding unnecessary cross-shard work can reduce resource demand, but the sources do not provide a general savings percentage. (medium confidence)

The ArchTenet author describes an unnamed production episode in which geo-sharding without region predicates and suitable indexes increased work across shards and increased the database bill. The article labels its pricing illustrative; this is not an independently audited cost benchmark. (low confidence)

Documents outside every configured zone range may reside on any shard. Regional placement therefore requires explicit coverage of all relevant geographic values, including newly introduced values. (medium confidence)

Defining zones and their ranges before sharding an empty collection enables initial placement consistent with those zones. Changing a populated collection’s zone mapping can require a period of redistribution, so new regional placement is not instantaneous. (medium confidence)

Zones determine which shards own a range; they do not alone guarantee that every replica stays in that geography. Atlas Global Cluster documentation describes distributing a zone’s shard members among its configured regions, so residency assessment must also inspect replica-region configuration. (medium confidence)

Zones also support assigning selected data to shards with suitable hardware. The cost opportunity is a placement policy matched to workload needs; neither the manual nor Percona’s example establishes a measured total-cost reduction. (medium confidence)

Zone ranges must use shard-key fields and include the compound key's prefix. For country-based placement, MongoDB's tutorial uses {country: 1, userid: 1}: country defines geographic groups, while userid contributes higher cardinality and lower frequency than country alone. (medium confidence)

Geographic zones can place data closer to the applications that use it, reducing network latency and overhead. This identifies a potential cost lever, but neither cited source quantifies a generally applicable financial saving. (medium confidence)

Percona warns that location-based sharding can produce data skew and require additional infrastructure for multi-site deployments. Its guidance recommends monitoring both per-shard data volume and query load; geographic grouping does not itself ensure even resource use. (low confidence)
